_about: Provenance for the hardware-derived constants that cross a session or
project boundary. WHY THIS EXISTS: on 2026-09-11 a correct attack law was
replaced by one 1.8x wrong, and the cause was not arithmetic -- it was a
method attributed to the wrong section. Three provenance errors happened
in one day; in every one the VALUE travelled correctly and where it came
from did not, because the value lives in the code and the provenance lived
in a comment above it. Peers quote the value.
The two fields that would have prevented that day are `convention` and
`subject`. A constant that says 'time to full level' cannot be silently
compared against a -3 dB reading, and a subject field makes 'one was a
synthesized sine and the other a resident sample' visible without reading
the live constant, so a constant cannot be changed without this file
failing. That is the point: the failure is what forces the provenance to
`provenance_gap: true` marks an entry whose method or subject nobody has
written down. It is a to-do, not a defect in the value -- but a constant
with no recorded convention is one misreading away from 2026-09-11.

entries.name: _AK_ATTAK1_TIME
entries.quantity: ATTAK1 byte -> seconds, t = a * exp(b * byte)
entries.convention: time to FULL level (the ramp is linear in amplitude)
entries.method: Hilbert envelope, line/plateau knee, 7 rungs, residuals -1.4%..+2.1%
entries.subject: synthesized CONSTANT-AMPLITUDE sine, 33 Hz, SUSTN1 99, probe note 24, velocity 80
entries.known_limits: CONFIRMED TO 0.3% AT ATTAK1 90 AND 99 by an independent capture path in a different session (s3ked §239, 2026-09-14), and independently supported by §141 (2026-08-20 -- a different session, method and rig) which agrees within 2% at ATTAK1 80, 90 and 99. THE FAST END IS NOT CONFIRMED: below about ATTAK1 70 the two paths still differ by 23%, cause unknown, and one path shows an unexplained 47 ms floor at ATTAK1 0. That is where the corpus's percussive attacks live. Fitted 60..99; below 60 is extrapolated and unmeasured. REPEATABILITY IS RUNG-DEPENDENT BY A FACTOR OF A HUNDRED: +-5% at ATTAK1 60 (8 takes), 0.03-0.04% at 90 and 99 (4 takes each). Short attacks contain few envelope steps, so a fixed jitter is a larger share of them. Quote the rung with the figure.
entries.supersedes: (0.00015, 0.10545) 2026-09-11, which was read at -3 dB through a 5 ms RMS window on a 33 Hz tone -- 1.41 x 1.26 = 1.78x slow
withdrawn_caveats: §236's program-dependence (the same byte giving a 33% different attack on a second program) was WITHDRAWN by s3ked §237 the same day. It never compared two programs: it compared one capture path against another, with the program riding along, because the same program had never been measured twice. Nine variables had been correctly eliminated from a comparison with no effect in it.

'The law may be out by up to 28%' stood here for 20 minutes and was wrong twice over: the disagreement was 9% across most of the range and 34% only at the fast end, and the +-5% repeatability it leaned on is specific to ATTAK1 60. Both figures had travelled here without their conditions.

The 9% path disagreement was RESOLVED by s3ked §239: JACK runs at 48000 and the newer analysis scripts had SR = 44100 hardcoded, so every absolute time through that path read 8.8% long. measure.py writes WAVs and reads the rate from the file, which is why the older path -- the one this law rests on -- could not make the mistake. Confirmed against a value known a priori rather than against another capture: the probe carrier read 961 Hz on MIDI note 84, and 961 x 48000/44100 = 1046.0 Hz against C6's 1046.5, a miss of 0.05%. ROOT CAUSE, which is worth more than the constant: captures were saved as .npz arrays with no sample rate in them and the rate was then supplied from memory by a separate script -- the data and the fact needed to interpret it were separated, and the fact was wrong. That is this file's own reason for existing, one level up.

THIS FIELD WAS REWRITTEN FOUR TIMES ON 2026-09-14, each time honestly and each superseded within the hour. Kept visible rather than tidied: the point of this file was never to be right first time, it was to make a correction land in one obvious place instead of in a comment nobody re-reads.

entries.name: _AK_RELSE1_RATE
entries.convention: a RATE over a span, not a duration
entries.known_limits: Fitted 45..99 only. Below 35 the fit collapses to r2 0.51-0.73 AND stops depending on the setting, which is the signature of measuring the rig's own tail rather than the envelope. Marked unmeasurable rather than filled in.

entries.name: _AK_DECAY1_RATE
entries.convention: a RATE over a span, not a duration

entries.name: AKAI_FILTER_LAW
entries.quantity: FILFRQ byte -> Hz, Hz = a * exp(b * byte)
entries.convention: the -3 dB corner, which is what every source format means by cutoff
entries.method: direct measurement of the -3 dB point
entries.known_limits: §54 claims the same quantity by another route (peak sits AT the corner, does not move with FILQ) and disagrees by 1.29x. That is an unexplained disagreement, not a definitional offset, and s3ked has it open with one sweep intended to yield both numbers. §139 is used because it measures the -3 dB point directly.

entries.name: _E4XT_ATK_SLOWDOWN
entries.quantity: multiplier applied to a requested attack before encoding
entries.convention: 1.0 means the writer targets the machine's -3 dB point, NOT its full traversal
entries.method: a CHOICE, not a measurement -- which point of a convex curve to match
entries.known_limits: THE RECORDED REASON IN THE SOURCE IS STILL WRONG AND IS SCHEDULED FOR REWRITE. It claims the machine agrees with `intends` 'at the same convention'; those are two conventions. Matching at full traversal instead would need ~1.17 -- as measured on ONE preset, spread across presets unmeasured. 1.4125 is a property of a LINEAR ramp and must not be carried here: the E4XT's is strongly convex, 28% delivered at its own nominal attack time (§ATTACKSHAPE).

entries.name: ENV_RATE_SWEEP_A
entries.method: extrapolated from a fit over bytes 60..100
entries.known_limits: EXTRAPOLATED, not measured, at byte 0 itself. The cross-check that supported this ladder read byte 89 as 10.1 s on one preset and 9.10 s on another -- an 11% disagreement recorded as agreement, corrected 2026-09-14 to 'the byte is the MAIN term, not the only term'. Neither cross-check row recorded its note or its preset. THE EXPLANATION PREVIOUSLY OFFERED HERE IS WITHDRAWN: this field said the 11% might be the E4XT's 'measured note-dependence of 1.25x across 55 semitones'. eosed §121 (2026-09-14) shows there IS no note-dependence -- the 1.25x was a fixed 5 ms detector on TRANSPOSED material. A note ladder plays one sample at many rates, so the material's own modulation stretches by 2^((origkey-note)/12) and a fixed window resolves a different number of sample-periods at every rung. Scale the detector with the playback rate and the effect goes flat (t90 ratio 0.962). The control that settles it: a preset with an INSTANT attack still read 0.060 s at note 16 against 0.020 s at note 64 -- a 3x note-effect on a rise that does not exist. So the 11% is unexplained again, and the paths it was blamed on are both cleared. Smoothing can CREATE a spread it cannot remove: the widest rate-scaled window here is 31.7 ms against a 2.570 s measurement, 1.24%, which cannot hide a 1.7 s effect but can manufacture one out of a 30 dB ripple crossing a threshold early.

entries.name: ENV_RATE_SWEEP_K
entries.quantity: natural-log step per rate byte, dB/s law
entries.known_limits: DISAGREES WITH ENV_RATE_K (0.0581) BY 2.8%, which is inside the noise of both fits, and nothing yet picks between them. The firmware route to settling it is CLOSED: EOS 4.61 and 4.70 ship as an LZEXE stub plus a packed floppy image whose decompressor lives in the E4XT's boot ROM (eosed §116, entropy + autocorrelation + 36 schemes + an XOR whose expected agreement was computed before running). It stays with the captures.

entries.name: ENV_RATE_A
entries.quantity: seconds at rate byte 0, time-alone law
entries.convention: a TIME, and only correct at the span the calibration used
entries.known_limits: Rate 0 is the deliberate 'instant' encoding and is NOT a point on this curve; `env_rate_to_seconds` must return 0 there. It used to return 0.031, and the commonest single round-trip difference over the E4B corpus was 'attack 0.0 -> 0.031' on 77.4% of zones.

entries.name: ENV_RATE_K
entries.quantity: natural-log step per rate byte, time-alone law

entries.name: ENV_LEVELBYTE_DB_INTERCEPT
entries.quantity: dB below the attack peak at level byte 0
entries.known_limits: Named for the BYTE deliberately: `ENV_LEVEL_DB_INTERCEPT` exists for the sustain-PERCENT law and silently shadowed this one when it was first written, so every reading came out 0 dB with no error.

entries.name: KRZ_ENV_TIME_GRID
entries.quantity: K2000 envelope-time display grid, seconds per editor step; time byte = steps(seconds) + 3
entries.convention: the EDITOR's step grid, so byte 3 is 0.00 s and the finest quantum is 20 ms
entries.known_limits: The 20 ms quantum is 1/50 s and has no relation to the 41.7 ms in §KRZENVLOOP (1/24 s) -- checked 2026-09-14 and recorded as coincidence. The 27 ms release floor that trips §KRZDBLZERO is 0.5 * 20 ms / (0.2 * 1.9): this grid, _REL1_TIME_FRAC and KRZ_RELEASE_FACTOR, and nothing from the machine.

entries.name: KRZ_RELEASE_FACTOR
entries.quantity: correction from the shared MPC value->seconds curve to the K2000's displayed release
entries.method: one pair: 2.63 s displayed against 1.39 s from the curve
entries.subject: AlphaPad #200
entries.known_limits: ONE OBSERVATION, ONE PROGRAM. 'roughly constant' is asserted in the source comment and is not measured across the range.

entries.name: KRZ_2POLE_F0_TO_3DB
entries.convention: converts the machine's f0 label to the -3 dB corner the model carries
entries.method: confirmed four ways: gain at the corner, the -3 dB crossing, an external instrument (the MPC, measuring the same quantity), and an A/B by ear
entries.known_limits: The 4-pole is DELIBERATELY not corrected by the same route; see KRZ_4POLE_F0_TO_3DB.

entries.name: KRZ_4POLE_F0_TO_3DB
entries.convention: converts the machine's f0 label to the -3 dB corner
